auditor: i18n-auditor (independent translation auditor; not the translation author)
fallback: none — the configured model deepseek/deepseek-flash was served for the whole audit; no provider fallback was used
independence: I did not author, translate, edit or review-to-completion any of the eight catalogues under audit, and I hold no write path to them: this receipt is the only file this run wrote. Every claim below was derived here — hashes from the files on disk with sha256sum, the delta from git diff 87b2eb12b5..3e887bb3b4 over src/i18n, placeholder and key-set facts by parsing the eight JSON catalogues, typographic facts by codepoint inventory of each catalogue against its own base revision, and the sibling-term comparisons by grepping the same locale's existing ui.browser strings rather than trusting recollection. Where a language judgement could have gone either way I checked a native-usage source before reporting it (vi 'Thẻ' is confirmed legitimate for a tab in Chrome's Vietnamese UI, so the vi finding is filed as a consistency break at minor, not as a mistranslation; ur 'سرگزشت' is attested in Urdu writing for browsing/search history, so no finding is filed against it). No catalogue byte was modified by this audit, and the receipt says nothing about rendered output, which it did not observe.

findings.observation: The guillemets are padded with ordinary spaces (U+0020) on both sides of the placeholder. Every other guillemet pair in this catalogue pads with NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE (U+202F): consent_request.agent_in, consent_request.the_agent_in_untitled_chat and webauthn_chooser.requesting_page. French typography wants a non-breaking space there, and in a narrow, ellipsised address row a plain space lets a line break strand the opening guillemet at the end of the line.
findings.evidence: value bytes: ...Rechercher <U+00AB><U+0020>{query}<U+0020><U+00BB> sur DuckDuckGo; the three existing pairs read <U+00AB><U+202F> ... <U+202F><U+00BB> (grep of the catalogue: 24 x U+202F, this key contributes none)
findings.disposition: fix with the suggested bytes; no meaning change

findings.observation: d'historique uses the ASCII apostrophe (U+0027), the only one in the whole fr ui.browser catalogue. The catalogue writes 125 typographic apostrophes (U+2019) across 86 keys, including its own neighbouring strings. ASCII apostrophe is also ICU MessageFormat's quoting character, so it is the one apostrophe form to keep out of message templates.
findings.evidence: counts over src/i18n/catalogues/fr/ui.browser.json: U+0027 = 1 occurrence in 1 key (this one); U+2019 = 125 occurrences in 86 keys

findings.observation: The 'marker — value' separator is a spaced single em dash (U+2014 with U+0020 on both sides). All six other em-dash strings in this catalogue use the Chinese double em dash '——' with no spaces, including the same pattern in browser_tab_strip.all_tabs_unshown ('所有标签页——{count…}') and browser_url_bar.home_destination. A spaced single Latin dash is visibly not Chinese typography in a row that renders constantly.
findings.evidence: dash inventory of zh-CN/ui.browser.json: 12 unspaced U+2014 (six '——' pairs) vs 1 spaced pair — the new key; see browser_tab_strip.all_tabs_unshown, browser_url_bar.home_destination, browser_url_bar.latest_download

findings.observation: The query is wrapped in ASCII straight quotes (U+0022). This is the only ASCII-quoted string in the ur catalogue: its eight other quoted insertions all use curly quotes “…” (browser_tab_strip.*, browser_consent_request.*, webauthn_chooser.requesting_page). ASCII quotes are bidi-neutral and take direction from their neighbours, so around an arbitrary user query inside an RTL run the pair is the least stable delimiter available; the curly pair is the form the rest of the locale already uses.
findings.evidence: counts over src/i18n/catalogues/ur/ui.browser.json: U+0022 = 2 occurrences in 1 key (this one); U+201C/U+201D = 8 pairs in 8 keys
findings.disposition: fix with the suggested bytes; the word order itself is correct and stays

findings.observation: 'Thẻ' is the only use of that word for a browser tab in the catalogue: 35 keys render tab as 'tab', including the tab strip itself (browser_tab_strip.new_tab = 'Tab mới', browser_tab_strip.close_tab = 'Đóng tab') and the hand-over dialog that names the same open tab (browser_hand_over_dialog.let_an_agent_use_this_tab = 'Cho tác nhân dùng tab này'). 'Thẻ' is a legitimate Vietnamese word for a tab (Chrome's own vi locale uses 'Thẻ mới'), so this is a same-product terminology split rather than a mistranslation: the row would say 'open card/tab' next to chrome that says 'tab'. Kept at minor for that reason.
findings.evidence: grep of vi/ui.browser.json: 'thẻ' = 2 occurrences, both new keys; 'tab' = 35 keys
findings.suggested: Tab đang mở — {title} / Tab đang mở
findings.disposition: fix by adopting the catalogue's established 'tab'; both new keys change together so the marker pair stays parallel

findings.observation: Guillemets «» are used nowhere else in this catalogue, which quotes user-supplied titles with ASCII double quotes in the five browser_tab_strip keys and with “” in the two consent/webauthn keys. Guillemets are RAE-correct as primary quotes, so this is a third-style consistency nit, not an error.
findings.evidence: es quote inventory: «» = 1 pair (this key), "…" = 5 keys, “…” = 2 keys
findings.suggested: Buscar "{query}" en DuckDuckGo — only if the catalogue wants one style for quoted user text
findings.disposition: no change required; record and leave to the implementer's judgement

findings.observation: 'Tìm' is the find verb this locale already uses for find-in-page ('Tìm trong trang', browser_url_bar.find_in_page and browser_find_row). 'Tìm kiếm' is the unambiguous web-search verb. The current text is idiomatic and understood, so this is wording only, and the alternative costs four more characters in a narrow row.
findings.evidence: vi/ui.browser.json: find-in-page keys render 'Tìm trong trang'; the search row is the only web-search string
findings.disposition: optional; accept as-is if row width is tight
